units.text: INT. HOLLOW OAK MARKET - NIGHT
A trunk wider than a barn, hollowed out and hung with lanterns.
Stalls climb the inner walls on rope ladders.
Fireflies drift between the rafters.
The air smells of resin and hot sugar.
At a low stall: ORSOLYA, 40s, apothecary, moth-wing scarves wrapped to the elbow, ink on her fingertips.
Sells lanterns.
None are lit.
BRANWICK, 60s, a retired knight whose armor is long gone, wears a farmer's coat that doesn't fit his shoulders.
He stands before the stall with his hat in his hands.
Walking light or hanging light?
units.name: ORSOLYA

units.text: Hanging.
units.name: BRANWICK

units.text: She lifts a small tin lantern.
He doesn't look at it.
Bigger.
units.name: BRANWICK

units.text: For a barn?
units.name: ORSOLYA

units.text: For a window.
units.name: BRANWICK

units.text: She sets down the tin one.
Lifts a larger one with a blue glass panel.
Blue's for waiting.
units.name: ORSOLYA

units.text: That one's fine.
units.name: BRANWICK

units.text: PIPKO, 9, ash on her cheek, apprentice, sits cross-legged behind the counter threading wicks.
She watches Branwick without pretending not to.
He bought a blue one last year.
units.name: PIPKO

units.text: Pipko.
units.name: ORSOLYA

units.text: Same shoes. Same hat. He turned it in his hands like that.
units.name: PIPKO

units.text: Branwick turns the hat in his hands.
Stops.
Lantern's broke. The window lets in a draft.
units.name: BRANWICK

units.text: The window.
units.name: ORSOLYA

units.text: Yes.
units.name: BRANWICK

units.text: She nods, as if this is a perfectly reasonable thing.
She wraps the lantern in cloth.
A third voice, from above: HAJI TESFAYE, 70s, a merchant lowering himself down a rope ladder with a basket of candles, one hand over the other.
Orsolya! The Duskwife says the wicks need wax by morning!
units.name: TESFAYE

units.text: Then she can have wax by morning.
units.name: ORSOLYA

units.text: Evening, Sir Branwick.
units.name: TESFAYE

units.text: Not "Sir."
units.name: BRANWICK

units.text: Evening, Branwick.
units.name: TESFAYE

units.text: Branwick counts coins into Orsolya's palm.
Too many.
She slides two back, firmly, and he pockets them without a word.
You have to light it from a flame that someone gave you. Not one you made.
units.name: PIPKO

units.text: I know the rule.
units.name: BRANWICK

units.text: Last year's was still burning when I walked past the barn.
units.name: PIPKO

units.text: Silence.
Orsolya reaches under the counter and takes out a stub of candle, already lit.
She offers it to him in a clay dish.
Mine. Take it.
units.name: ORSOLYA

units.text: He takes the dish with both hands, as if it might spill.
Tesfaya sets down the basket and starts to hum something old.
How much for the wax?
units.name: BRANWICK

units.text: Nothing. Bring the dish back.
units.name: ORSOLYA

units.text: I will.
units.name: BRANWICK

units.text: He settles his hat on his head, tucks the lantern under his arm, and walks off carefully through the hanging lights.
He will.
units.name: PIPKO

units.text: Thread your wicks.
units.name: ORSOLYA
